speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS) will consider (i) mandatory CCTV recordings in areas where pets are handled or housed in pet grooming facilities and (ii) requiring licensed operators to retain such footages for investigation purposes, to support accountability and transparency.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Failure to meet minimum standards stipulated under the Code of Animal Welfare may be used as evidence for enforcement action.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do have a few supplementary questions for both my Parliamentary Questions (PQs).

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For my first PQ, I would like to ask, are the current standards for supervision of pets during grooming sessions, particularly when they are secured in holding areas or cages, whether the Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS) would review the protocols for this to prevent prolonged unsupervised confinement that may result in distress or worse, injury or fatality?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And the other supplementary questions for this PQ are: what are the current processes and response time for handling complaints of suspected negligence in pet businesses?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And how can AVS improve public reporting channels and investigation process to ensure timely follow-up?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The whole point is really, how to, first of all, report and also, how can pet owners be more aware of businesses that have had complaints and may not have followed protocols.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But more importantly, are there going to be tighter protocols, for when they are in confined areas or unsupervised?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For my second PQ, I would also like to ask, apart from penalties – because that is after the fact and when once pet is injured, or I think the distress I have had for my residents and many pet owners who have shared that it can be extremely distressing and so, rather than penalties, which are good deterrents, but really prevention – so, will AVS consider introducing mandatory certification or competency requirements for pet groomers?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And more importantly, skills training to ensure proper animal handling, not so much the grooming, but the animal handling and safety protocols, and more importantly emergency response when the pets are injured.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Will the Ministry also review the licensing conditioning for pet grooming businesses to incorporate minimum supervision requirements and emergency preparedness protocols?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is a lot more than two supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First of all, as I mentioned to the Member, we are reviewing the ABA and we are getting feedback from Members, as well as members of the public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are reviewing under the review of the ABA, the regulatory regime for pet sector activities and this includes pet grooming businesses and the other areas in which the Member has highlighted.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the Code for Animal Welfare, which I mentioned earlier on, this is for specific to the pet industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This Code of Animal Welfare specifies minimum standards and best practices for pet businesses and pet groomers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we are looking at all of these reviews under the review of the ABA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Currently, there are already levers for NParks to take action and we will take all of the feedback into regard.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If members of the public or the Member herself comes across any reports, please feel free to contact AVS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I have gotten the number here – it is 1800 4761 600.
